Customer raised questions about latency vs cost tradeoffs, quantization compatibility with their on-prem hardware, and SOC2/VPC concerns. Agreed on POC and benchmarks with their prompts.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-28 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Alex Morgan (Saturn CTO), Priya Patel (Saturn ML), Sam Torres (Saturn Security), Ella Chen (Product)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'll kick things off. Priya and Marco are on from the SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Alex Morgan: Good, thanks. Excited to see the model catalog, we had some internal questions about which open models we can use for clinical summarization.
[00:15] Jordan Lee: Perfect, that's what we'll cover — catalog, perf profiles, and the compatibility matrix for Dedicated and Private. Quick agenda: demo the console, show benchmarks, then dig into quantization/hardware compat.
[00:30] Priya Shah: Quick note — feel free to interrupt, we'll show live latency numbers but they vary with sequence length and batch.
[00:40] Alex Morgan: Yep noted.
[00:45] -- Demo start / Redwood Console --
[00:50] Marco Diaz: (screen share) Alright here's the model catalog. You can filter by task, license, verified perf. For Saturn's use-case I filtered to summarization models and open licenses. See this row — LlamaX-13B-int8-optimized, verified on A100 and T4.
[01:10] Priya Patel: Sorry, is LlamaX Llama 2 fork? The naming in our notes is messy.
[01:16] Marco Diaz: Yeah, it's a community open model variant, we vendor it as LlamaX in the catalog. Transcription note — sometimes names get munged in the export.
[01:27] Sam Torres: Security first — what about data residency if we use hosted vs dedicated? We need to ensure PHI never leaves our VPC.
[01:36] Priya Shah: Great question. For hosted we have strict controls but for PHI we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated in a single-tenant pool with strict network controls and KMS integration. We'll attach SOC2 and KMS papers after this call.
[01:50] Alex Morgan: OK. Can you show the compatibility matrix? We have some in-house infer infra (NVIDIA H100 and some older T4s).
[01:59] Marco Diaz: Sure — opening the compatibility tab. You can see a matrix per model: supported quantizations (FP16, INT8, LLM.int8, AWQ), recommended hardware, and notes on kernel availability. For example, LlamaX-13B-int8-optimized shows INT8 support on Ampere and Hopper kernels, but on T4 you'll see degraded perf so we provide fallback FP16 variant.
[02:25] Ella Chen: What about memory & KV cache implications for long clinical notes? We often have 8k-16k sequences.
[02:32] Priya Shah: Longer sequences increase KV cache use and can change batching efficiency. For 8k you may want a variant compiled with attention tiling and optimized kernels — you can see perf profiles per sequence length in the benchmark tab.
[02:45] -- Benchmarks / Perf Profiles --
[02:48] Marco Diaz: Pulling up the benchmark profile for the model. We include latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens estimate. These are measured across sequence lengths and batch sizes. Important to consider: microbenchmarks are done on standardized inputs; your real prompts often shift the tradeoff.
[03:10] Alex Morgan: On cost estimates, how do you compute 'cost per 1k tokens'? Does that include infra and amortized model warmup?
[03:17] Marco Diaz: It's a normalized estimate: GPU runtime + amortized lifecycle costs, with assumptions noted in the spreadsheet. We can provide the raw measurements so you can re-calc with your cloud prices.
[03:27] Sam Torres: Any support for HSM KMS? We require customer-managed keys.
[03:31] Priya Shah: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and Dedicated can be configured to use your KMS via IAM roles and key wrap. We'll send the implementation guide.
[03:42] -- Questions from Saturn on model selection --
[03:45] Priya Patel: Our ML team is concerned about hallucinations in open models. Do you have evals tied to quality metrics or prompt sets?
[03:53] Priya Shah: We do — Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts. In the catalog each model has eval summaries and links to sample eval suites. For clinical use we recommend a small in-house eval set (we can help) and continuous regression alerts.
[04:08] Alex Morgan: If we run a POC, can we pin a model version and route with fallbacks? If Dedicated capacity is saturated, what's the fallback?
[04:18] Marco Diaz: Yes, you can pin versions and define routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, region-first. Fallbacks include routing to a compatible FP16 variant or a hosted lower-tier if you permit. Fallback policies are configurable per route.
[04:33] -- Perf tradeoffs demo (live numbers) --
[04:36] Marco Diaz: Running a sample summarization prompt (we'll use a synthetic 2k token note).
[04:41] [00:05 of micro-test] Marco: On H100 we see p50 210ms per token, p95 860ms, tokens/sec ~1200 with batching 8. On T4 same model INT8 gives tokens/sec ~280 but latency p95 jumps.
[04:58] Alex Morgan: That matches our internal experience — big drop on T4 for INT8. So compatibility matrix is important.
[05:05] Priya Shah: Exactly — our catalog flags recommended quant and hardware combos and shows kernels supported.
[05:12] -- Discussion: quantization formats and tradeoffs --
[05:15] Priya Patel: Can you explain AWQ vs LLM.int8 and impact on quality?
[05:19] Marco Diaz: AWQ is more aggressive compression, lower memory, usually faster on commodity GPUs but can regress quality on some tasks. LLM.int8 tends to retain quality but may need runtime kernel support. Our perf notes include recommendation tags per task.
[05:35] Sam Torres: From security angle, do quantized checkpoints leak anything different? Any additional risk?
[05:40] Priya Shah: Not significantly different; checkpoint confidentiality is managed the same. For on-prem we recommend encrypted storage and KMS. We'll include the data handling doc.
[05:50] -- Console: Model comparison & release notes --
[05:53] Marco Diaz: Here you can compare two models side-by-side — accuracy proxies (BLEU/ROUGE-ish for summarization), latency curves, and kernel support. Notice how we tag models 'Redwood-verified' when we've run our long tail of tests.
[06:10] Alex Morgan: How often do those verification runs happen?
[06:14] Marco Diaz: Monthly for popular models, ad-hoc when a new kernel or quant comes out. We also surface known regressions.
[06:22] -- Customer: integration questions (API) --
[06:24] Alex Morgan: For integration, we use an internal inference gateway. Do you expose streaming and function calling?
[06:31] Jordan Lee: Yes, Redwood API supports streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. SDKs are available in Python and Node.
[06:36] Priya Patel: Any rate limits or quotas we should know for Dedicated?
[06:40] Priya Shah: Dedicated is configurable — you'll get reserved concurrency and optional burst. We can propose an autoscaling policy for your expected throughput.
[06:47] -- Deep-dive: benchmarks with customer prompts --
[06:49] Marco Diaz: For the POC we'll ask for three canonical prompt sets — short triage notes, medium visit summaries (~1-2k tokens), and long discharge summaries (~8-12k). We'll run benchmarks on both Dedicated (H100 pool) and a hosted variant to show latency vs cost and quality comparisons.
[07:08] Alex Morgan: Timeline — how quickly can you spin up that benchmark?
[07:11] Priya Shah: If you share prompts by Friday (2026-04-30) we can run an initial micro-bench within 3 business days, so results by 2026-05-05.
[07:20] -- Objection / procurement note --
[07:22] Ella Chen: Our procurement will likely push for an SLA and a pilot price. What's the pilot model?
[07:27] Jordan Lee: We typically offer a 4-6 week pilot on Dedicated or Private with usage credits. We'll include a pricing sheet and terms in the follow-up.
[07:37] -- Security specifics --
[07:38] Sam Torres: For SOC2, do you have an attestation or only self-reported documents? Also need audit logs per user.
[07:46] Priya Shah: We have SOC2 Type II and we can provide the report under NDA. Audit logs and token-level tracing are available via Redwood Console, and we can set retention policies.
[07:58] Sam Torres: Good. Also need details on SSO/SAML and RBAC.
[08:03] Jordan Lee: We support SSO (SAML/Okta), and RBAC for team roles. We'll include a setup guide.
[08:11] -- Routing and graceful degradation --
[08:12] Marco Diaz: One feature customers like: automatic fallback policies that switch to a lower-cost FP16 variant if INT8 kernels aren't available in a region. That keeps the app online with minor perf changes.
[08:25] Alex Morgan: How do you measure quality regression in fallbacks?
[08:29] Priya Shah: Redwood Optimize can tie evals to routes. If a fallback leads to a quality drop over a threshold, we alert and optionally pause the fallback.
[08:39] -- Pricing notes --
[08:40] Jordan Lee: Quick note on pricing: hosted is usage-based per token/embedding; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit and different unit economics; Private is enterprise licensing. We'll include example numbers tailored to your throughput.
[08:55] Alex Morgan: Can you share a spreadsheet that maps tokens/sec to hourly cost for H100 vs T4 vs hosted?
[09:01] Jordan Lee: Yes — compatibility/benchmark spreadsheet includes that table.
[09:05] -- Demo wrap and live Q/A --
[09:07] Priya Patel: How do we handle model updates? We want stable inference during a rollout.
[09:12] Marco Diaz: Rollouts: canary then full, with automatic rollback on errors or quality regressions. You can pin model versions to routes to avoid surprises.
[09:21] Alex Morgan: One more on data retention — logs retention and token-level cost visibility.
[09:26] Priya Shah: You can set retention windows and export logs; Console shows per-route token costs.
[09:33] -- Practical POC scope discussion --
[09:35] Jordan Lee: Proposed POC: 4 weeks, run benchmarks on your three prompt sets on Dedicated H100 pool and hosted fallback, capture latency/cost and quality metrics, include regressions alerts and a short runbook for switching variants.
[09:47] Alex Morgan: Sounds good. Procurement will need pricing — please include pilot discount.
[09:52] Jordan Lee: We'll include that.
[09:55] -- Final recap and next steps --
[09:56] Jordan Lee: Recap: we'll send compatibility matrix + benchmark template, Priya will run micro-bench on Dedicated, Alex will share prompts by 4/30, Sam will confirm compliance ask. Schedule POC kickoff week of 5/4.
[10:12] Alex Morgan: Thanks, looks actionable.
[10:15] Sam Torres: Thanks — appreciate the KMS notes already.
[10:18] Marco Diaz: One last note — we'll also include notes about kernel-specific flags if you end up compiling in-house.
[10:24] Jordan Lee: Great. We'll follow up with the deck and attachments. Thanks everyone.
[10:30] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional name munging (LlamaX), timestamps approximate, some technical terms abbreviated.

References/Links mentioned: Redwood model catalog (link in follow-up), compatibility spreadsheet (will be attached), SOC2 report (NDA), demo deck (link).
questions: Can models be pinned and do you support rollbacks?
What's the expected perf of INT8 on T4 vs H100?
How quickly can Redwood run benchmark on customer prompts?
